aboutH2: Executive Medical Solutions: outpatient addiction treatment in Winnipeg
intro: Executive Medical Solutions (EMS) is a private outpatient addiction program at 3408 Roblin Boulevard in Charleswood, in southwest Winnipeg. There are no beds. You keep living at home and going to work, and you come in for counselling and groups, or join groups online when you cannot make it in person.

The program pairs weekly one-to-one counselling and daily groups with medical care. A psychiatrist assesses co-occurring mental illness, usually in your first week, a pharmacist reviews your medications, and people with opioid use disorder can be assessed for Suboxone. EMS asks for a four-month commitment and builds the full program around one year.

pillars.title: Psychiatry, pharmacy and Suboxone assessment
pillars.body: Psychiatric wait times in Manitoba can run to many months. EMS says its clients usually see the program psychiatrist in their first week and always within four weeks. Dr. Jeffrey Waldman has practised psychiatry since 2003, holds a subspecialty in forensic psychiatry and is certified by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Manitoba to prescribe Suboxone. He looks at depression, anxiety and other conditions that run alongside drinking or drug use. Bloodwork can be ordered, a pharmacist reviews medications, and you can keep your own pharmacy or use the one EMS partners with.

pillars.title: Weekly counselling and daily groups
pillars.body: Each client has a one-to-one counselling session every week. The counsellors work from a trauma-informed base and borrow from DBT, CBT and other addiction methods. On top of that, EMS runs one to three groups a day, and each week the groups take apart a different recovery topic. The centre recommends at least four groups a week and says people who come more often tend to do better. Yoga, somatic breathwork and mindfulness sessions are part of the mix, and EMDR therapy can be arranged quickly for trauma.

pillars.title: A team that includes an Elder
pillars.body: Alongside the psychiatrist, the team page lists counsellor and recovery coach Jennith Guertin, who holds a master's in counselling psychology, and social worker Christy Perreaux, who has 17 years in case management and crisis work. Laura Lourenco, a nurse, is the client relations contact. Ovide Caribou, a Cree Traditional Fire Keeper and Spiritual Healer, leads sweat lodge ceremonies for those who want them. Several staff write openly about their own recovery, and the centre notes it sits on Treaty 1 Territory.

overview: EMS describes itself as an outpatient addictions treatment program for people who want to work on recovery while their life carries on around them. Its reasoning is practical: you learn to handle your triggers, stress and social life in Winnipeg as they really are, and you go home each day to try out what you learned.

The centre treats alcohol and drug addiction, including opioid use disorder, and it puts weight on trauma. Its website says substance use problems are more common in people who lived through childhood adversity, so every client is approached as someone who may carry trauma. The recovery.com profile lists the program as founded in 2019.

faqIntro: Answers come from Executive Medical Solutions' own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Executive Medical Solutions a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. It is a private outpatient addiction program in Winnipeg, and you keep living at home and working while you take part. There are no beds or overnight stays. You come in for individual counselling and group sessions at 3408 Roblin Boulevard, and you can join groups virtually when you cannot get there.

Every client gets weekly one-to-one counselling plus access to one to three groups a day. The counselling draws on DBT, CBT and other addiction-specific methods with a trauma-informed approach. The program also offers psychiatric assessment for co-occurring mental illness, pharmacist consultation, Suboxone assessment, rapid access to EMDR therapy, and yoga, breathwork and mindfulness sessions.

Executive Medical Solutions asks for a four-month commitment, and the full program is designed to run for one year. The centre says research links about 90 days of treatment while abstinent with better long-term recovery, and that the first month of a community program often is not fully abstinent. It suggests at least one individual session and four groups a week.

faqs.q: How much does Executive Medical Solutions cost?
faqs.a: The centre's website lists $16,000 plus GST for the first four-month commitment, with a $500 plus GST intake deposit that goes toward the program cost. Recovery.com lists that as $4,000 a month for the first four months and about $1,000 a month after that. Months after the first four cost less, and the centre asks you to contact it to confirm current prices.

faqs.q: Is it covered by Manitoba Health?
faqs.a: The program is private pay. Neither the centre's website nor its recovery.com profile lists Manitoba Health coverage or direct insurance billing. If you hope to claim part of it through workplace or extended health benefits, ask your insurer what it covers for psychiatry, social work and counselling before you pay the deposit.

faqs.q: Can I get Suboxone or medical care for co-occurring mental health conditions?
faqs.a: Yes, through assessment. Psychiatrist Dr. Jeffrey Waldman is certified by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Manitoba to provide opioid agonist therapy (Suboxone), and the centre offers psychiatric assessment, usually in the first week of the program. Bloodwork can be ordered to check for medical problems linked to substance use, and you can use your own pharmacy or the one the centre partners with.

faqs.q: Does Executive Medical Solutions offer detox?
faqs.a: Its website does not describe a medical detox or withdrawal unit, and there are no beds on site. If you drink heavily every day or use opioids, benzodiazepines or other drugs with risky withdrawal, talk to your doctor or Manitoba's public withdrawal services before you start. The centre's Suboxone assessment is a separate service for opioid use disorder.

The centre says it runs continuous intake so there is no wait time, and you can begin when you are ready. To start, you send a consult request form, book a free consult call and then complete the new client intake form. A deposit is taken before an intake counsellor gathers your information.
Yes. The centre says its program includes family members who want support or information. How involved they are is decided case by case, and the choice is yours.

It is at 3408 Roblin Boulevard in Charleswood, in southwest Winnipeg, about 20 minutes by car from downtown. Headingley is roughly 15 minutes west, Selkirk and Steinbach are each about an hour away, and Portage la Prairie is about an hour along the Trans-Canada. Google lists wheelchair accessible parking.
